# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no standardised first-touch-to-first-class experience; inconsistent induction depth, form capture, goal-setting timing
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no documented win-back triggers, exit interview protocol, or pause-vs-cancel decision tree
- **Member Check-ins** – no cadence, ownership, or conversation framework for retention touchpoints (30/60/90 day, post-pause, low-attendance)
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – no documented data handling, consent capture, deletion/export request process, or audit trail (legal/compliance risk)
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no career progression, skill certification, or performance review cycle for coaches
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no peer or manager-led feedback mechanism on class delivery, coaching cues, energy, safety
- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – no standardised weekly duties beyond teaching (admin, member check-ins, floor presence, feedback loops)
- **Referral Programme** – no incentive structure, tracking mechanism, or claim process
- **Milestone Achievements & Member Outcomes** – no system to track/celebrate progress, measure coaching impact, or use as retention/marketing lever
- **Supplies & Sundries ordering** – no reorder triggers, vendor management, or budget accountability
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – no escalation pathway for common member complaints, technical issues, or safety incidents

---

# **Needs updating**

- **Member Pause SOP** – likely exists but probably missing: pause-to-resume re-engagement cadence, pause duration limits, win-back messaging
- **Coaches 19/22** – 3 SOPs missing; likely gaps in: performance management, absence/cover protocol, payroll/timekeeping accuracy

# Service Menu Execution — The Forge

**1. Start with your highest-revenue services first**
Don't map everything. Interview your top 3-5 coaches about what they actually sell most (personal training packages, group classes, nutrition add-ons, challenges). Price these first, get them right. Everything else follows. You'll move faster and capture the money that matters.

**2. Create two separate documents — and be ruthless about what coaches see**
Coaches need: service name, duration, price, what's included, upsell opportunities, commission structure. Members need: service name, benefit, price, how to book, what to expect. Don't dump your full pricing/margin strategy on members. Coaches need the business logic; members need the outcome.

**3. Run a 30-minute "pricing reality check" with your top-performing coach**
Show her your draft menu. She'll immediately spot if pricing is too low (leaving money on the table) or positioned confusingly (loses sales). One person's gut check beats weeks of guessing. Also shows coaches you're including them in decisions — builds buy-in.

**4. Test the menu live before finalizing**
Use it with 10 new inquiries this week. Track which services people ask about, which confuse them, which they push back on price-wise. One real conversation beats assumptions. Update based on actual pushback, then lock it.

**5. Build a simple "service decision tree" for coaches**
When a member walks in, what questions do they ask first? Map the conversation flow on one page so coaches recommend consistently. This prevents undercutting and ensures members get to the right offer.

**Insights**

1. **You've found product-market fit but July was an anomaly, not a trend.** July's 215 leads at £2/lead looks like a budget spike or algorithm exploit that didn't hold. August stabilised at 82 leads/£5 CPL—still dramatically better than Apr–Jun (where you were bleeding £6–£21 per lead with zero sales), but a 62% drop in volume month-on-month. The close rate stayed healthy at 29%, so the leads are real.

2. **Your unit economics only work at volume.** At 29% close rate, you need leads cheap enough that 3 duds + 1 sale = profit. At £5/lead you're breaking even or barely ahead per sale (£29 income minus £5 × 4 leads = £9 margin before opex). July at £2/lead gave you breathing room. August is tight.

3. **Something changed in August—either budget got cut, or Meta's algorithm cooled after July's spike.** The spend dropped 18% (£515→£424) and leads halved. That's not natural drift; it's either a deliberate pause or the hot audience from July got exhausted.

---

**Actions**

1. **Immediately test audience expansion to recapture July's scale.** July hit 215 leads on similar spend. Audit what changed: Did you broaden targeting? Was there a specific lookalike or interest that fired? Rebuild that exact stack—and layer in 2–3 new cold audiences (e.g., fitness interests outside gym category, women interested in wellness/mental health, local Belfast female audiences aged 25–45 with higher income). Run these at 20% of budget to find the next high-volume segment.

2. **Drop cost-per-lead as the target; optimise for sales instead.** Your Apr–Jun obsession with CPL left you with zero conversions. Switch Meta's campaign objective from Lead Gen to Conversions (track trial sign-ups as purchase events). Let the algorithm spend more on leads that look like your 29% converters, even if CPL ticks up to £6–£8, because you'll get more closeable prospects.

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO BRIEF

## REVENUE — CRITICAL ISSUES

• **Rev/member has collapsed to £99 in August (down from £144 in July, down from £131 average Jan–Mar).** You're adding members (164 vs 137 in July) but revenue per head is falling sharply. Root cause: either heavy discounting on new joiners, or existing members not paying full rate. Audit your membership tiers and new-member pricing immediately — you should be hitting £130+ per member. If new members are below £100, you're onboarding at unsustainable LTV.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** (vs 3–6% norm). That's 17 members lost in one month on a base of 133 — likely the studio relocation disruption. You've recovered (5.5% Aug), but monitor churn weekly now; any spike above 6% needs root-cause action (staff gaps? class cancellations? messaging failure?).

• **Last 3 months (Jun–Aug) averaged £17,363/month revenue vs prior 3 (Jan–Mar) at £14,508** — solid 19.7% growth in absolute terms. But you're *not* translating member growth into revenue growth at the same rate. July was your best month (£19,764). You need to understand what drove July and replicate it: was it a promotion? Full classes? Upsells (PT, merchandise, class packs)?

• **No visible ancillary revenue** (PT sessions, retail, class packs, nutrition plans). At 137–164 members, you have a captive base. Introduce a £15–25/month add-on tier or one-off PT bookings; even 20% uptake at £20/member = +£550/month gross.

---

## EXPENSES — HIGH SPEND vs REVENUE

• **Cash outflows are erratic and often exceed revenue:** Aug cash out was £28,693 on £16,160 revenue (176% ratio). Jun was £20,644 on £15,765 (131%). Exclude April relocation, but you're running a structural cash burn 15–30% of months. Break down that £28,693 in August: wages, rent, supplies, utilities? If any single line is >40% of revenue, flag it. **Most likely culprit: payroll.** At 164 members and £16k/month revenue, you cannot afford more than £8–10k/month in fixed wages (staff + your salary). What are actual wages + on-costs in Aug?
